# Step 2.229 — A correction keeps what it replaces

## Builder 1: below the screen

**What exists.** A reopen of a game entered by hand (`reopen-game.ts`, `reopen-own-result.ts`) keeps the game's lines in its correction's `before.sheet` (`kept-sheet.ts`: ids, jersey number, played, seconds, counts; with capture mode and overtime), whenever it has lines (T-365). The saves after it (final score only, score within, forfeit) still clear the lines (S-27 stands); kept lines are a document, never counted. Command `games.put_sheet_back` (`put-sheet-back.ts`, `games.correct`, input `{ gameId, version, reason }`) restores the newest correction's sheet and result, writes a correction of its own and announces `games.finalized` (T-366). Errors: `game-not-found`, `changed-since-read`, `not-allowed`, `game-not-decided`, `result-overturned`, `no-sheet-kept`, `newer-save`. Port `games.newestCorrection` (query `find-newest-game-correction.ts`; memory, standings, imports and the web stand-in world). Migration `0029_a_correction_keeps_the_sheet.sql`: `before` up to 4 MB (`npm run db:types`: no change). Pending decisions T-365, T-366; P7 §5.2 corrected.

**Passed.** `sheet-put-back.test.ts` (5, seen failing first): final score only and forfeit, then put back: every line, standings rows, totals and the game as before the reopen; first correction unchanged; activity has each act once; no name in a correction; refused after a newer save, twice, from an old page, with no sheet. Core vitest (games, standings, imports: 661), schema `game-corrections` (seen failing first) and migrations, isolation (377), role-matrix rows for put back and reopen. `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `format:check`.

**What builder 2 builds.**

- In `apps/web/src/features/games-area`: on a decided game whose newest correction kept a sheet and is the reopen (the command's own rule; read it through a new read or the game's row), offer "Put the sheet back as it was" with a reason box, posting `games.put_sheet_back` with the version seen. Gone once something newer is saved. A refusal `newer-save` or `no-sheet-kept` says in plain words that something newer was saved, so the sheet can no longer be put back; `changed-since-read` reads the game again. Only for people who may correct games.
- A read for the offer, if the screen needs one, gets its own role-matrix row and isolation case (rule 9); `games.newestCorrection` is already in the store.
- Text in `packages/site/src/messages/en/` (the area's file): the button, the reason label, each refusal, and the activity line for `games.put_sheet_back` (`apps/web/src/server/activity-messages.test.ts`).
- Rule 9 lists: page-step rows in `scripts/check-web-shell.mjs`, the harmful-text test (the new reason field), `database-event-handlers.test.ts` if wired.
- A browser test of the done test: reopen a box score, save a final score only, put back: lines, standings and totals as before; the activity log has each act once; the same after a forfeit; put back after a newer save refused in plain words.

**Fails now, for builder 2 first.** `apps/web/src/server/activity-messages.test.ts` ("English words for every command that writes an entry"): `games.put_sheet_back` has no activity message yet. The rest of that run passed: core and `apps/web/src/server`, 309 of 310 files, 3283 of 3284 tests.

**What I distrust.**

- `fence-filter-check find-newest-game-correction`: the league filter SURVIVED. A correction's game id names one league's game (the foreign key pairs them) and row security hides the rest, so no case can tell; it stays as a fence.
- The put back's own correction makes the public "Corrected" mark show (S-81 compares each correction's result with the next), though the result ends as it was. The area 5 or 6 lead should say whether that is wanted.
- A put back restores lines for players who may have left the team since; it checks no roster (R-17 allows them).
- The web stand-in world's `newestCorrection` was added but not exercised by a test.

## Builder 2: the screen, the public mark, the fence

**What exists.** The game's own page in the Games area (`box-score-page.tsx`) offers "Put the sheet back as it was" with a reason box (`ReopenForm` with `kind="put-back"`, marked `data-put-back-form`), for whoever may correct games, only while the put back would be allowed: read before the tap by the new read `games.read_sheet_put_back_offer` (`read-sheet-put-back-offer.ts`), which follows the command's own rule, now one function (`sheet-put-back-rule.ts`, used by `put-sheet-back.ts` too). It posts the game's version and a request token (`putSheetBackAction`, `run-box-score-action.ts` `put-back`). Refusals in plain words (`admin.boxScore.putBackError.*`): `newer-save`, `no-sheet-kept`, `game-not-decided`, the reason; a page drawn before something newer was saved is refused as `changed-since-read`, then the offer is read again and the sentence says what happened. These refusals are said beside the form without drawing the page again (the offer would vanish with the sentence). Activity words for `games.put_sheet_back` (plain and named). T-367.

**The lead's ruling (S-98).** `correctedMarkDate` reads each correction's `after`: a correction that leaves the game decided is a put back; it ends the reopen it undid (that reopen's next final is the result the put back left) and marks nothing itself. So a put back to the result before the reopen leaves no mark from it; an earlier correction that changed the result keeps its mark and date; a later reopen is judged as any other. `find-game-corrected-date.ts` selects `after`; the stand-in world already held it. P7 (S-81 paragraph) corrected; pending S-98.

**The fence.** `find-newest-game-correction` now has an `arrange` (a fixed reopen correction of the target's upcoming game, inside the target's fence): `fence-filter-check` on that file: caught, 0 problems (it SURVIVED before, as builder 1 said).

**Pinned lists.** Role-matrix row and isolation case for the new read; `activity-messages.test.ts` (the read listed as a read); harmful text: the put back's reason is in `NOT_COVERED`, typed by `sheet-put-back-test` instead. No new page or route, so no page-step row; no event handler.

**Passed.** `corrected-mark.test.ts` (3 new, seen failing first: "expected '2030-12-07' to be undefined"), `sheet-put-back.test.ts` (1 new: the offer), `problem-keys.test.ts` (1 new); core games and standings, `apps/web/src/features/games-area`, `activity-messages`, `database-event-handlers` (87 files, 659 tests); role matrix and isolation (6 files, 637); `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`; `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`. Browser `sheet-put-back-test` (30 checks): a box score typed; reopened, saved as a final score only, put back: every box of the grid, the public standings and stats as before, the log has each act once, the public page no "Corrected"; the same after a forfeit; an old page's put back refused with the "something newer" sentence, its reason (markup) kept as text; a scorekeeper sees the game's page without the offer.

**What I distrust.**

- `fence-filter-check find-game-corrected-date` (I changed that file): both of its league filters SURVIVE, and did before this step. Each shadows the other (the game is read first with its filter, the corrections with theirs), so no case can tell; it is not on the excused list. The lead should excuse it or reshape the query.
- The browser test compares the public standings and stats pages' whole text; the core done test compares the rows and totals themselves.
- The forfeit's "Yes" waits one second first, as `saves-keep-test` does (a quicker "Yes" is taken as a double tap).
- `npm test` (all of `tests/*.test.mjs`), `npm run test:web` and the whole browser chain were not run.

## Independent review

**High.** None found.

**Medium.**

- A game tracked live since its reopen can still be put back. A reopened box score is `scheduled`, so a scorekeeper may open a scoring session on it (`scoring-session.ts` 89 to 92) and end it with plays; no correction is written, so the reopen stays newest and the offer shows. The put back (`put-sheet-back.ts` 48 to 90; `sheet-put-back-rule.ts` 19 to 28 checks no plays and no capture mode) then writes the old lines and `captureMode: 'box'` over a game that keeps its plays and state, with the sheet's score, not the plays'. A later reopen sees plays (`reopen-game.ts` 56) and rebuilds the lines from them. Read, not run. Fix: refuse while the game has plays or is `live` in capture.
- A second reopen hides the kept sheet for good: reopen, final score only, reopen again, save. The second reopen finds no lines, keeps no sheet, and the put back says `no-sheet-kept`, though the first correction still holds every line and nothing reads it (the builder's own test asserts it, `sheet-put-back.test.ts` 188 to 206). By the plan's words ("until something newer is saved") but against A-5 for an admin who reopens again to fix the slip. The lead decides: carry the sheet forward on a reopen of a game with no lines, or warn there (2.56).
- Fence: `node scripts/fence-filter-check.mjs find-game-corrected-date` gives 2 SURVIVED, 2 problems (exit 1). The PR gate (`ci.yml`) does not run it; the weekly Fence sweep (`.github/workflows/fence-sweep.yml`) does and would fail. It was caught in the 2.224 sweep (`2.224-sweep.tsv` 21); 2.56 and this step changed the file since. Reshaping is sound, excusing is not: two excuses for one query would leave neither filter tested. Read only from `game_corrections` joined to `games` on (league_id, id) with one league filter (no rows means no mark), and give the isolation case an `arrange` with a correction on the target's game.

**Low.**

- The offer never ends on a box score corrected on purpose (reopen, fix one line, save). One tap months later undoes the fix, and the sheet it replaced sits in the put back's `before` with no way back (T-366 as written). It wants a warning line.
- A person deleted between the wrong save and the put back: the correction keeps only the id, as T-220 says history does, so that holds. But `purge-binned.ts` 85 to 97 does not look at kept sheets. A binned person with no lines, totals or roster entry left can be purged, and the put back then fails on `player_game_stats_person` instead of a plain refusal. A binned person who is not yet purged gets their line back, and it counts. Unlikely (roster entries stay, R-17). Not run.
- T-220 (no names) rests on core's writer alone: the database does not check the shape of `before.sheet`. No test that `before` over 4 MB, or `after` over 16 KB, is refused (`game-corrections.test.ts` 123).
- Browser test: `publicText` (`sheet-put-back-test.mjs` 87 to 97) does not check that the page is the one asked for. "Standings as before" and "no Corrected" would pass on two equal error pages. The stats check is live, because it must first see a change.

**Holds.** Every line, the standings rows and the totals come back (the core done test compares them whole; a score within takes the forfeit's and the final's path, `record-score-within.ts` 37 to 38, and is not tested apart). Kept lines are no `player_game_stats` rows and count nowhere. The jersey format is held by the database check, and a correction holds no names. A correction stays unchangeable: the 0009 trigger is untouched and the app role may only select and insert (tests 169 and 181). 0029 checks the rows already written again, all under 16 KB. A double tap, an old page, two admins and a put back while reopened are each refused. Roles and another league are covered by role-matrix `gameRows` and the isolation cases. S-98: reopen, change, final, reopen, wrong save, put back keeps the first mark and its date, and a slip that is put back leaves none.

**Broken by hand, then restored.** The put back dropped `fouls`: both round trips of `sheet-put-back.test.ts` failed. The `newer-save` refusal was removed: "is done once" and "is offered" failed. The skip of a put back in `correctedMarkDate` was removed: three `corrected-mark.test.ts` cases failed.
